test_cases.Test Description: Verifies reset defaults and masked read/write behavior across GPIO per-pin control, interrupt, group IO control, group DOUT, and group DIN registers using predefined data patterns and read/write masks. The least significant bit is ignored during default comparisons, and specific registers are excluded from default and/or R/W phases per skip controls.
test_cases.Remarks: Default compare clears the least significant bit before comparing with documented defaults. Certain group input/output registers are skipped for default and/or write/read checks as defined by skip arrays to avoid false mismatches related to input/level behavior.
Test Steps / Procedure: Start the test sequence.

Reset-default verification phase: For each register in the ordered list [GPIO_8..GPIO_39, GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1, INTR1_INTR_EN1, INTR1_INTR_STS1, INTR2_INTR_EN1, INTR2_INTR_STS1, GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4, GPIO_DOUT_GROUP1..GPIO_DOUT_GROUP4, GPIO_DIN_GROUP1..GPIO_DIN_GROUP4]:
- If the register is marked as skipped for default checking, proceed to the next register.
- If the register is not readable per its mask, proceed to the next register.
- READ the register.
- Clear the least significant bit of the read value and compare the result with the documented default for that register; record a default-mismatch error if not equal.
Write/read verification phase across six data patterns (all-ones, alternating A, alternating 5, F5 pattern, A5 pattern, upper-half ones): For each pattern in order:
- For each register in the ordered list:
-- If the register is marked as skipped for write/read, proceed to the next register.
-- If the register is not writable per its mask, proceed to the next register.
-- WRITE the register with (pattern AND the register’s write mask).
- For each register in the ordered list:
-- If the register is marked as skipped for write/read, proceed to the next register.
-- If the register is not both writable and readable per masks, proceed to the next register.
-- READ the register and apply the read mask to the value.
-- Compute expected = (pattern AND write mask AND read mask) OR ((bitwise complement of write mask) AND read mask AND the documented default for that register).
-- Compare the masked read value with the expected value; record a write/read-mismatch error if not equal.
Finish: If both the default-mismatch count and write/read-mismatch count are zero, report pass; otherwise report fail.

Validation / Acceptance Criteria: For each register included in the default check, the read value with the least significant bit cleared must match the documented default; any mismatch is a failure.

For each included register and for each data pattern, the masked read value must equal: (pattern AND write mask AND read mask) OR ((bitwise complement of write mask) AND read mask AND documented default); any mismatch is a failure.
Overall pass condition: zero default-mismatch errors and zero write/read-mismatch errors.

test_cases.Test Description: Configures GPIO_8 through GPIO_39 as inputs with negative-edge interrupt detection enabled, generates a falling edge per pin using an external pad control address, and validates per-pin raw status, masked group status, and system interrupt clearing using an interrupt service routine with a bounded wait.
test_cases.Remarks: A bounded wait loop (timeout 5000 units) is used for each pin. The wait flag is armed before generating the edge to prevent races. Platform/system interrupt enable and raw-status clear are performed via system registers.
Test Steps / Procedure: Start the test sequence.
Enable the platform interrupt for the target instance and enable the system-level interrupt output via INTR_EN1.
Drive the external pad control at 0xA0243ffc to all high to establish a known initial state.

Configure each per-pin control register GPIO_8 through GPIO_39 for input mode with negative-edge interrupt detection enabled and clear the per-pin raw status; insert a short wait after each configuration.
For each bit position i from 0 to 31 (mapping to GPIO_8..GPIO_39):
- Clear the corresponding raw interrupt bit in GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1.
- Enable only that bit in INTR1_INTR_EN1 and insert a short wait.
- Arm the interrupt wait flag.
- Drive 0xA0243ffc to all high, wait briefly, then drive low for only the target bit to create a falling edge.
- Enter a bounded wait loop with timeout 5000 units; poll until the wait flag is cleared by the interrupt service routine; if the loop expires, record a timeout error for that pin.
In the interrupt service routine:
- Immediately drive 0xA0243ffc to all high to restore a known state.
- Read the current per-pin register (corresponding to GPIO_8 + i) and verify the input indicator shows low after a falling edge; record an error if not low.
- Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify that the bit for the current pin is set; record an error if not set.
- Clear the per-pin raw status by writing the per-pin control register to request raw clear while keeping input mode.
- Clear the corresponding group raw bit by writing to GPIO_INTR_RAW_STCLR1.
- Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify the group status is now zero; record an error if not zero.
- Clear the system-level raw status for this instance via RAW_STCR1 and clear the platform interrupt.

test_cases.Test Description: Enables positive-edge detection for GPIO_8 through GPIO_39, sets all groups to input mode, generates a per-pin rising edge using an external pad control address, and validates masked group status and system raw status clearing using an interrupt service routine with a bounded wait.
test_cases.Remarks: A bounded wait loop (timeout 2000 units) is used per iteration. The wait flag is armed before generating the rising edge. The group interrupt is masked during ISR service, per-pin raw status is cleared for all pins, and system raw status is verified by readback.
Test Steps / Procedure: Start the test sequence.
Enable the platform interrupt for the target instance and enable the system-level interrupt output via INTR_EN1.
For each per-pin control register GPIO_8 through GPIO_39, enable positive-edge interrupt detection.
Set group IO control registers GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP1..GPIO_IO_CTRL_GROUP4 to input mode for GPIO_8..GPIO_39 and insert a short wait.
Enable all bits in INTR1_INTR_EN1.
For each iteration i from 0 to 31:
- Drive 0xA0243ffc to low to create a baseline and wait briefly.
- Arm the interrupt wait flag.
- Drive 0xA0243ffc to all high to generate a rising edge.
- Enter a bounded wait loop with timeout 2000 units; poll until the wait flag is cleared by the interrupt service routine; if the loop expires, record a timeout error and exit the loop.
- Optionally drive 0xA0243ffc low and wait briefly to prepare for the next iteration.
In the interrupt service routine:
- Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and mask group interrupts by writing zero to INTR1_INTR_EN1 during service; require that the group status is nonzero upon entry.
- For each per-pin control register GPIO_8 through GPIO_39, request raw-status clear for the pin and wait briefly.
- Read INTR1_INTR_STS1 and verify the group status is now zero; record an error if not zero.
- Clear the system-level raw status via RAW_STCR1 and verify by reading RAW_STCR1; re-enable all bits in INTR1_INTR_EN1 and clear the platform interrupt.

In the interrupt service routine, INTR1_INTR_STS1 must be nonzero upon entry with positive-edge configuration; after per‑pin raw clears for all pins, the group status must be zero.
System-level raw status must be cleared successfully via RAW_STCR1 and verified by readback; group interrupt must be re-enabled after service.
